title: BRICKSTORM_Backdoor_Investigation_498
description: Investigate and respond to the BRICKSTORM backdoor malware compromise in the target network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The target network has been compromised by a sophisticated backdoor malware named BRICKSTORM. This malware uses advanced techniques to evade detection, including SOCKS proxying, multi-layered web service communication, and varied command execution. Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident. This training will help you develop skills in service discovery, persistence mechanism analysis, and file investigation techniques.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the target host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The target host's IP address is `192.168.50.5`.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the target host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The target host's IP address is `192.168.50.5`.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service running on the target host. What is the name of the suspicious service running on the target host?
levels.solution: To identify the suspicious service, you can use the `systemctl list-units --type=service` command to list all running services. Look for any services that seem unusual or unauthorized. The suspicious service in this scenario is the `updatemgr.service`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Start by understanding the context of the problem. You are looking for services that do not belong to the standard system configuration.

hints.title: Methodological Hint
hints.content: System services can be listed using systemd commands. This will help you identify any unauthorized services.

hints.title: Command Hint
hints.content: Use the `systemctl list-units --type=service` command to list all running services.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot. What is the persistence mechanism used by the suspicious service?
levels.solution: To determine the persistence mechanism, investigate systemd services and timers. The suspicious service `updatemgr.service` is started by the `updatemgr.timer` timer, which is set to run minutely. This is the persistence mechanism used by the suspicious service. Use the `systemctl list-timers` command to list all systemd timers and identify the `updatemgr.timer`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Persistence mechanisms often involve timers or cron jobs that start services automatically. Focus on systemd timers.

hints.title: Methodological Hint
hints.content: Systemd timers can be listed using specific commands. This will help you identify how the service is started automatically.

hints.title: Command Hint
hints.content: Use the `systemctl list-timers` command to list all systemd timers.

levels.title: Locate Executable or File
levels.content: Locate the executable or file associated with the suspicious activity. What is the path to the executable or file associated with the suspicious service?
levels.solution: To locate the executable or file associated with the suspicious activity, correlate the service with its associated files. The executable associated with the `updatemgr.service` is located at `/usr/local/bin/lab-checkin.sh`. Use the `systemctl status updatemgr.service` command to find the associated files.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Executables associated with services can often be found in standard binary directories or custom paths specified in the service configuration.

hints.title: Methodological Hint
hints.content: Service status commands can provide detailed information about the associated files and executables.

hints.title: Command Hint
hints.content: Use the `systemctl status updatemgr.service` command to find the associated files.
